hook: SCP-8595 is an ordinary American cockroach that is convinced it is a restaurant critic, and it would rather starve than eat something beneath its standards. Most of the article is its reviews, written in the weary voice of a professional food writer who never once admits to being an insect. Keep an eye on the footnotes as you read; they quietly contradict what the reviews describe.
whyItMatters:
It's a comedy built on one mismatch, and the joke grows through the Foundation's ever more lavish efforts to please its smallest resident. The reviews double as a parody of food criticism, since every restaurant fails in a different direction: too bare, too clever, too much.

The containment notes keep a completely straight face the whole way through, which is what makes the escalation land.
thingsToNotice:
Each restaurant is a bigger build than the one before: a sterile café serving a single apple, a minimalist concept space in an empty dorm, then a full steakhouse with a Michelin-starred chef, custom panelling, imported cutlery and two researchers trained as waiters. The footnotes show how much the critic misses, since its twist on nachos was a ring of Doritos, the blue seasoning it adored was mould, and the deconstructed BLT came with Ritz crackers. Small slapstick moments slip in too, like the roach tumbling into its wine glass and having to be fished out.

The punchline is the last venue, which is simply the site's dumpster placed in an empty supply closet. After a little over two hours inside, the critic hands out its only five-star rating, with a one-word review.
